tips.title: Start the homework habit now
tips.body: Don't wait for September. Even 20 minutes a night in Grade 8 makes Grade 9 way easier.
tips.why: A habit you already have is one less new thing to learn when everything else is new.

tips.title: Get a calendar and actually use it
tips.body: Put tests, practices, and due dates in it. Once it's all written down, your head feels a lot lighter.
tips.why: Tests and assignments love to land in the same week. A calendar shows you that before it happens.

tips.title: Write your goals down
tips.body: A goal in a journal is way harder to forget than one in your head. Keep it somewhere you'll see it.
tips.why: Writing it down turns a wish into a plan you can check on.

tips.title: Don't leave things to the last night
tips.body: Big assignments sneak up on you. Break them into small pieces and do one piece at a time.
tips.why: Small pieces feel easy. One giant all-nighter feels terrible and usually shows in your mark.

tips.title: Talk to your teachers
tips.body: If you're confused, ask. They'd rather help you early than see you fail a test.
tips.why: Teachers can't help with a problem they don't know about.

tips.title: Join a team or a club
tips.body: It's the fastest way to make friends in a new school. You already have something in common.
tips.why: Clubs and teams give you a group before you even know your way around.

tips.title: Be social, even if it's awkward
tips.body: Everyone is new in Grade 9. Say hi to the person beside you.
tips.why: Most people are just as nervous as you and are happy someone talked first.

tips.title: Keep your binder and backpack organized
tips.body: Losing a handout the day before it's due is the worst. One folder per class fixes most of it.
tips.why: Less time looking for stuff means more time actually getting it done.

tips.title: Find a study spot that works
tips.body: Somewhere quiet, with your phone in another room. Use the same spot every time.
tips.why: Your brain learns that this spot means focus time.

tips.title: Balance school and your life
tips.body: Grades matter, but so do friends, sports, and sleep. Make time for all of them.
tips.why: If you burn out in October, the rest of the year is way harder.

goals.title: Get good grades
goals.doable: Study 30 minutes on school nights and hand everything in on time.

goals.title: Make new friends
goals.doable: Talk to one new person each week in class or at lunch.

goals.title: Join a school sport
goals.doable: Find the try-out dates in the first two weeks and put them in your calendar.

goals.title: Join a school club
goals.doable: Go to one club meeting in September, even just to see what it's like.

goals.title: Be social
goals.doable: Say hi to the person beside you in every new class on day one.

skills.name: Time management
skills.what: Planning your time so things get done before they're due, not the night of.
skills.example: When my first tests all landed in the same two weeks, I started putting every due date in a calendar. It saved me.
skills.try: Write down every due date you have this month in one place.

skills.name: Organization
skills.what: Keeping your stuff and your work where you can find it.
skills.example: I gave each class its own folder. No more digging through my backpack for a handout.
skills.try: Clean out your backpack and give each subject its own folder.

skills.name: Communication
skills.what: Asking for help and saying what you need, to teachers and friends.
skills.example: I was lost in one unit, so I stayed after class and asked. Ten minutes fixed what would have been a bad test.
skills.try: Ask a teacher one question you've been too shy to ask.

skills.name: Good study habits
skills.what: Studying a little at a time, in a good spot, without distractions.
skills.example: Studying 30 minutes a night with my phone in another room worked way better than cramming.
skills.try: Study for 20 minutes tonight with your phone in a different room.
